reason: B offers the more specific, substantive, and testable intervention, with a composition/process baseline, measurable wear and corrosion outcomes, boundaries, and prior evidence supporting TiB2-mediated hardening and a boron-dependent passive-film effect. Its key weakness is that the cited evidence shows different boron levels optimizing wear and corrosion and does not establish simultaneous tribocorrosion, so a boron dose series—not a single post hoc “optimal” level—is needed to test the proposed joint mechanism decisively.
